1. Let O be origin. Denote vectors a=OA, b=OB, c=OC, p=OP.
Since O is centroid of equilateral base, a+b+c=0.
Since P not in base, p is not in span of a,b,c (or independent in 3D).
2. Express S,R,Q:
OS = OP + PS = p + m(a-p)=m a+(1-m)p.
OR = n b+(1-n)p.
OQ = k c+(1-k)p.
3. Since O,S,R,Q are coplanar, there exist real α,β,γ with α+β+γ=1 and α OS + β OR + γ OQ =0. (Affine dependence.)
4. Substitute:
α m a + β n b + γ k c + [α(1-m)+β(1-n)+γ(1-k)] p =0.
5. Decompose into base part and p part. Because p is independent of base plane, the coefficient of p must vanish:
α(1-m)+β(1-n)+γ(1-k)=0. (Equation I)
And the base part must be zero:
α m a + β n b + γ k c =0. (Equation II)
6. Since a,b,c are coplanar and satisfy a+b+c=0 with no other relation, Eq II implies the coefficients are proportional to (1,1,1). Thus there exists t with αm=βn=γk=t.
7. From Eq I:
α - αm + β - βn + γ - γk = (α+β+γ)-3t=1-3t=0, so t=1/3.
8.

Also α=t/m, β=t/n, γ=t/k. Sum α+β+γ=1 gives:
(1/3)(1/m+1/n+1/k)=1 -> 1/m+1/n+1/k=3.
9. Therefore (mn+nk+km)/(mnk)=3, so mnk/(mn+nk+km)=1/3.
Box.

Let \(O\) be the origin. Write

\[
\mathbf a=\overrightarrow{OA},\quad 
\mathbf b=\overrightarrow{OB},\quad 
\mathbf c=\overrightarrow{OC},\quad 
\mathbf p=\overrightarrow{OP}.
\]

Since \(O\) is the center of the equilateral base \(ABC\),

\[
\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c=\mathbf 0,
\]

and \(\mathbf p\) is not in the base plane.

Because

\[
\overrightarrow{PS}=m\overrightarrow{PA},
\]

we have

\[
\overrightarrow{OS}
=\mathbf p+m(\mathbf a-\mathbf p)
=m\mathbf a+(1-m)\mathbf p.
\]

Similarly,

\[
\overrightarrow{OR}=n\mathbf b+(1-n)\mathbf p,\qquad
\overrightarrow{OQ}=k\mathbf c+(1-k)\mathbf p.
\]

The plane passes through \(O\), so the three vectors \(\overrightarrow{OS},\overrightarrow{OR},\overrightarrow{OQ}\) are linearly dependent. Thus there exist scalars \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\), not all zero, such that

\[
\alpha \overrightarrow{OS}+\beta \overrightarrow{OR}+\gamma \overrightarrow{OQ}=\mathbf 0.
\]

Substitute the expressions above:

\[
\alpha m\mathbf a+\beta n\mathbf b+\gamma k\mathbf c
+
\bigl[\alpha(1-m)+\beta(1-n)+\gamma(1-k)\bigr]\mathbf p
=\mathbf 0.
\]

The base-plane part and the \(\mathbf p\)-part must each vanish:

\[
\alpha m\mathbf a+\beta n\mathbf b+\gamma k\mathbf c=\mathbf 0,
\]

\[
\alpha(1-m)+\beta(1-n)+\gamma(1-k)=0.
\]

Using \(\mathbf c=-\mathbf a-\mathbf b\), the first equation becomes

\[
(\alpha m-\gamma k)\mathbf a+(\beta n-\gamma k)\mathbf b=\mathbf 0.
\]

Since \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\) are independent,

\[
\alpha m=\beta n=\gamma k=:t.
\]

Then the second equation gives

\[
\alpha+\beta+\gamma-3t=0.
\]

But

\[
\alpha=\frac{t}{m},\qquad \beta=\frac{t}{n},\qquad \gamma=\frac{t}{k},
\]

so

\[
t\left(\frac1m+\frac1n+\frac1k\right)=3t.
\]

For the nondegenerate case in which the given fraction is defined, \(m,n,k\neq 0\), so \(t\neq 0\). Therefore

\[
\frac1m+\frac1n+\frac1k=3.
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{mn+nk+km}{mnk}=3,
\]

so

\[
\frac{mnk}{mn+nk+km}=\frac13.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac13}
\]
